''''Stone rods''' (せきぼう, sekibō) are a type of polished {{ill|Stone tool|ar|الأدوات الحجرية|bn|পাথরের যন্ত্র|cs|Kamenný nástroj|da|Stenredskab|de|Steingerät|el|Λίθινο εργαλείο|eo|Ŝtona ilo|fa|ابزار سنگی|fr|Pierre taillée|he|כלי אבן|id|Alat batu|it|Manufatto litico|ja|石器|ka|ქვის იარაღები|ko|석기|ku|Amûra kevirî|mn|Чулуун хэрэгсэл|nl|Stenen werktuig|no|Steinverktøy|pl|Narzędzia kamienne|ps|ډبرينې وسيلې|pt|Ferramenta de pedra|ru|Каменные орудия|simple|Stone tool|sv|Stenverktyg|tr|Taş alet|uk|Кам'яні знаряддя|ur|پتھروں کے اوزار|vi|Công cụ đá|zh|石器|zh_min_nan|Chio̍h-khì|qid=Q479257|lt=Stone tool}} from the [[Jōmon period]] in Japan. They are believed to represent [[phalluses]] and are associated with [[:en:Rituals|Rituals]] and [[shamanistic practices]].Yamada 2019: 204

The largest known stone rod is the {{ill|Great Sekibō of Kitazawa|ja|北沢大石棒|qid=Q18457535}} in {{ill|Sakuho, Nagano|arz|ساكوهو|ceb|Sakuho Machi|es|Sakuho|fa|ساکوهو، ناگانو|fi|Sakuho|fr|Sakuho|hy|Սակուխո|it|Sakuho|ja|佐久穂町|ko|사쿠호정|ms|Sakuho, Nagano|my|ဆခုဟိုမြို့၊ နဂါနို|pl|Sakuho|ru|Сакухо|sv|Sakuho|tl|Sakuho, Nagano|tr|Sakuho|uk|Сакухо|uz|Sakuho (Nagano)|zh|佐久穗町|qid=Q1203700|lt=Sakuho, Nagano}}, measuring 223 cm in length and 25 cm in diameter.

== Overview ==
In a broad sense, "stone rods" encompass various rod-shaped stone artifacts, including [[stone swords]] and [[stone daggers]]. In a narrower sense, they often refer specifically to large stone rods.Tori 1924 These artifacts have been found throughout Japan, from [[Kyushu]] to [[:en:Hokkaidō|Hokkaidō]].

Prefecture|qid=Q120730|lt=Kyoto Prefecture}}.Matsui, Oshita & Tamura 1997Takahashi & Kondo 2011 These findings suggest that the use of stone rods as ritual objects was adopted as a cultural practice across different regions.Oshita 2001

Some stone rods have been found near the [[:en:hearths|hearths]] of dwellings, often showing signs of heat damage or discoloration. This indicates their use in fire-related [[:en:Rituals|Rituals]]. Ritual practices involving stone rods are thought to symbolically represent the phases of male genital arousal, sexual activity, and post-ejaculatory flaccidity through actions such as striking, heating, and breaking the rods. The prevalence of broken stone rods in archaeological sites has led some researchers to attribute symbolic meanings to this practice, though others remain skeptical.Gotō 1999

Stone rods were also used as burial goods, suggesting multiple [[:en:shamanistic|shamanistic]] or ritualistic purposes.Yamada 2019: 206Taniguchi 2006
